messages:
maya (pm): heads up — got a priority ask from ACME: they want per-tenant routing + per-route cost caps so they can route some requests to cheaper quantized variants. they said they'll push spend if we ship fast

sam (sales): +1 from acme, they said other vendors are pitching per-tenant price controls as a 'must have' for renewal 

oliver (design): quick question — is this a purely UI/affordance work (controls + labels) or do we need routing primitives in the runtime?

tj (eng): runtime work for sure. we need: 1) tenant routing rules that map routes -> model variant, 2) enforcement of cost caps (tokens/time window), 3) metrics for billing hooks. infra impact: moderate. can prototype a shim that rewrites requests to a variant pool.

anika (infra): also need to consider cache/keying. per-tenant routing increases cache miss rate unless we shard KV cache. that's a potential perf cost.

maya (pm): proposal: ship a minimal 'soft routing' MVP: admin API to set route->model-variant plus a per-route daily budget cap that triggers fallback to default variant. no UI for now, API-only for pilot customers. can we spike this week?

pj (eng): (sorry jumping in) if we go API-first we can reuse existing policy-eval path and add a small policy table per-tenant. low risk.

tj (eng): spike estimate: 3 dev days to wire policy + fallback, 2 days test/telemetry, 1 day ops docs. rollout plan: K=1 pilot tenant behind feature flag, 2 week pilot.

sam (sales): sounds good. acme wants pilot by EOW next week. is that realistic?

maya (pm): EOW is tight. we can offer an accelerated pilot with manual config (engineers set rules for them) — reduces delivery risk and still validates demand.

oliver (design): for the manual pilot we should provide a simple templated JSON snippet they can hand us. small UX alignment but nothing heavy.

maya (pm): snippet example to use: 

```
{
  "tenant_id": "acme-123",
  "routes": [
    {"path": "/chat", "variant": "gptq-6b", "daily_token_cap": 500000},
    {"path": "/summarize", "variant": "base-13b", "daily_token_cap": 200000}
  ]
}
```

tj (eng): that works. fallback rule: if cap reached -> route to `default-1` variant and emit billing alert.

anika (infra): add telemetry keys: `rbac.tenant`, `routing.variant`, `cap_hit` so we can analyze hit rates. we'll need a short retention window for pilot logs.

maya (pm): launch criteria for pilot: 1) manual config applied for ACME, 2) metrics surface in console (cap usage + fallback rate), 3) rollback path documented, 4) SLOs unchanged for default tenant traffic.

tj (eng): I'll put a PR up with the policy table POC today. will tag @maya + @anika.

deploy-bot: deploy queued for feature/shim-routing -> staging (build 5821) :shipit:

sam (sales): if pilot goes well we scope UI + automated billing integration in Q3. keep me posted so I can manage ACME expectations.

maya (pm): agreed. TL;DR: API-first manual pilot this week, automated UI/billing in next cycle if signal is positive. thanks team :rocket:

oliver (design): will draft the one-page config doc template after standup and share in this thread.

pj (eng): two quick followups: 1) are we comfortable with the compliance surface for per-tenant rules? 2) who owns the rollback runbook?

maya (pm): compliance: @security needs final signoff but pilot is internal-managed config so low surface. rollback runbook: ops + eng pair, @anika owns orchestration steps.

sam (sales): ACME PM asked about SLA changes if we route to lower-cost variants — we should prep a short note clarifying that fallback may have different latency/quality, not covered by existing latency SLA.

maya (pm): noted. add to pilot brief.

tj (eng): tagging this as `prio:urgent` for the week. I'll update the PR link in this thread when ready.

maya (pm): perfect. thanks everyone.
